mainTopic: רב's ruling to follow the unnamed משנה over a ברייתא, and whether a mother animal nurses a baby that is not her own (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, בכורה, אותו ואת בנו, the pig following a ewe)
overview: The גמרא asks why רב said both 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם' and 'the הלכה follows the whole chapter.' It answers that the separate statement shows 'the whole chapter' backs the unnamed משנה that matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and that a disagreement found only in a ברייתא is not a real dispute. It then quotes that ברייתא: a nursing animal bought from a גוי, where the first opinion worries she may be nursing a baby that is not hers, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we assume she is the mother. Next the גמרא asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means only that nursing proves she gave birth, or that the baby is surely hers. That difference matters for lashes under אותו ואת בנו. Three proofs are brought and all are pushed off. Then רבי יוחנן rules that a ewe followed by a pig-like animal is exempt from בכורה, but the animal may not be eaten until אליהו comes. After several challenges, the גמרא explains that the הלכה surely follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but it is unclear whether he holds that a mother animal may nurse another's baby, even one of another species. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a question of רבי יוחנן that supports this, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why did רב need to mention רבי יוסי בן המשולם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב had to say the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, since he already said the הלכה follows the whole chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the statement 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one of רב's statements looks extra. If the הלכה follows the whole chapter, that should already cover רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב made two statements: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, and the הלכה follows the whole chapter. The general statement seems to include the specific one. So the גמרא asks what the specific statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling
Why do I need it? This asks why something is said when it seems extra.

phrases.english: 'The halakha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam'
why do I need it?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's separate statement that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general statement 'the הלכה follows the whole chapter' should already cover it, so the specific statement looks extra.

steps.title: Without it, we would have misread 'the whole chapter'
steps.stepSummary: Had רב said only 'the whole chapter,' we would have thought he meant רבי יוסי בן המשולם's two rulings. We would also have thought that a disagreement in a ברייתא counts as a real dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רב had only said 'the הלכה follows the whole chapter,' I would think he was referring to רבי יוסי בן המשולם. 'Whole chapter' would just mean that רבי יוסי said two things. I would also think that a disagreement found in a ברייתא counts as a real disagreement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by describing the mistake we would have made. It imagines רב saying only the general statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'whole chapter' could be read as covering only רבי יוסי בן המשולם's two rulings. On that reading, רב would not be backing the unnamed משנה where a ברייתא disagrees. That would suggest a ברייתא disagreement is enough to make a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
The whole chapter
He is standing on, meaning he is referring to
Two (things)
A disagreement that appears only in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mistaken reading, the הוה אמינא. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Had he said 'the halakha follows the whole chapter,'

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָמַר הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: and not said 'the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם קָאֵי,
phrases.english: I would say: he is referring to Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,
and what does 'throughout the whole chapter' mean?
that Rabbi Yosei said two rulings,
and a disagreement in a baraita is a real disagreement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by showing what we would have wrongly assumed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that each statement is needed to block a misreading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Whole chapter' would refer only to רבי יוסי בן המשולם's two rulings, and a disagreement in a ברייתא would count as a real dispute.

steps.title: The separate statement shows that a ברייתא disagreement does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב stated רבי יוסי's הלכה on its own. This shows that 'the whole chapter' refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, which the unnamed משנה follows, and that a disagreement found only in a ברייתא is not a real dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב told us the הלכה follows רבי יוסי separately. This teaches that 'the whole chapter' refers to the case of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and that a disagreement in a ברייתא is not considered a real disagreement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. Since רבי יוסי already has his own statement, 'the whole chapter' must be talking about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי יוסי covered separately, 'the whole chapter' must also cover the unnamed משנה that matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view. The other opinion disagrees with him only in a ברייתא. רב still rules like the משנה, so a disagreement found only in a ברייתא does not count as a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught us, meaning he said it to make a point
It is not a real disagreement

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a disagreement that appears only in a ברייתא does not override the unnamed משנה in this chapter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a rule about how to decide הלכה: an unnamed משנה is followed even when a ברייתא records a disagreeing view.

phrases.english: He taught us 'the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei' —

phrases.aramaic: לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן דְּאַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָאֵי,
phrases.english: to teach us that he is referring to the case of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and a disagreement in a baraita is not a real disagreement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by replacing the mistaken reading with the correct one.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The whole chapter' includes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, which the unnamed משנה follows, and a disagreement found only in a ברייתא is not a real dispute.

steps.title: Which ברייתא is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברייתא contains the disagreement with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to show us the actual ברייתא it has been talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has only mentioned 'a disagreement in a ברייתא.' Now it asks for the source so we can see the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Which ברייתא is it?

phrases.english: What is the baraita?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא where the first opinion disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: The ברייתא of the nursing animal bought from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the next calf is a ספק בכור, because an animal may nurse a baby that is not its own. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we assume the nursing animal is the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone buys a nursing animal from a גוי. The next one born after that is a בכור only out of doubt, because an animal may feel pity and nurse a baby even if it never gave birth. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the matter stays as we assume it to be, meaning the animal is the nursing baby's mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it was asking about. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion matches the unnamed משנה, and the first opinion disagrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion worries that the nursing animal may not be the baby's mother. If so, she may never have given birth, and her next calf could be a real בכור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts the simple assumption that she is the mother, so her next calf is not a בכור. רב rules like him, because the unnamed משנה follows his view and the disagreement appears only in this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Nursing (an animal feeding a baby)
A firstborn out of doubt
Feels pity, here meaning it nurses a baby that is not its own
The matter stays as we assume it to be

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says the next calf is a ספק בכור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is not, and since the unnamed משנה follows his view, רב rules like him.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One who buys a nursing animal from a gentile,
the one born after it is a firstborn out of doubt,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the baby she is nursing now. Her next calf might be her first.

phrases.english: because she may feel pity and nurse
even though she has not given birth.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
the matter stays as presumed.
phrases.notes: We assume the nursing animal is the baby's mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מְנִיקָה מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא about a nursing animal bought from a גוי, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion.

steps.title: A second case: young found nursing in the flock in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a farmer who finds males nursing from older mothers and females nursing from first-time mothers does not worry that the young switched mothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the same way, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used to say: Someone goes into his flock at night and sees about ten or fifteen animals giving birth. Some are giving birth for the first time and some are not. The next morning he finds the males nursing from the mothers who had given birth before, and the females nursing from the first-time mothers. He does not need to worry that the baby of one mother went over to another mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from step 5 and adds another case where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל assumes that the nursing animal is the real mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a male born to a first-time mother is a בכור. If the males nurse from older mothers and the females nurse from the first-time mothers, then no בכור was born, as long as we trust the nursing. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we trust it and do not suspect that a male from a first-time mother moved over to an older mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A flock of animals
Animals giving birth for the first time, whose male baby would be a בכור
Literally 'hanging on.' Here it means nursing from
He does not need to worry about it

steps.confusionAlert: Males nursing from the older mothers is not the important part. The key is that the first-time mothers are nursing females, so they gave birth to females and there is no בכור.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say:
One who enters into his flock at night
and saw about ten or about fifteen animals,
first-time mothers and ones that are not first-time mothers, giving birth,
the next day he got up early and found
males nursing from the ones that are not first-time mothers,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets, תְּלוּיִין.

phrases.english: and females nursing from the first-time mothers —
he does not need to worry

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ.
phrases.english: that perhaps the baby of this one went over to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that answers step 4, with another case of the same principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts nursing as a sign of who the mother is, so no בכור is suspected in the flock case.

steps.title: What exactly does 'the matter stays in its presumption' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means that only an animal that never gave birth won't nurse, so one that did give birth might nurse a stranger, or that an animal only ever nurses its own young.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said 'the matter stays in its presumption.' Does he mean that an animal does not show mercy and nurse unless it has given birth? Then where it has given birth, we do worry that it might nurse another animal's baby. Or perhaps he means that an animal shows mercy only to its own baby and never to a baby that is not its own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question about the exact reasoning behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read him. Option 1: nursing only proves that the animal gave birth at some point, and it might be nursing a stranger's baby. Option 2: nursing proves that this particular baby is its own. Either way the animal has given birth, so the next baby is not a בכור. The difference shows up elsewhere, which the next steps explain.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
The matter stays in its assumed status
Shows mercy, which here means letting a baby nurse
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ דְּקָאָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: 'the matter stays in its presumption' that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵינָהּ מְרַחֶמֶת אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יוֹלֶדֶת —
phrases.english: does it mean that it does not show mercy unless it has given birth —
so where it has given birth
we worry that it may show mercy to a baby not its own,
or perhaps: it shows mercy to its own,
but to one that is not its own it does not show mercy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the reasoning behind the ruling quoted in steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an animal that has given birth ever nurse another animal's young?

steps.title: Why does this question matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the two readings make.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we care, since either way the animal has given birth and its next baby is not a בכור. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the laws of בכור, both readings lead to the same result. So the גמרא needs to find a different area of הלכה where the two readings would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? In what case?
What comes out of it, meaning the practical difference

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the question in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two readings give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: lashes for slaughtering a mother and its baby
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether someone who slaughters the nursing animal and the baby it nurses on the same day gets lashes for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether he gets lashes for slaughtering it, because of 'it and its young.' If you say an animal nurses only its own baby and not a stranger's, he gets lashes. But if you say it also nurses a baby that is not its own, he does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and points to the prohibition of אותו ואת בנו as the case where the two readings matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes require certainty that the two animals really are mother and baby. If an animal nurses only its own baby, nursing proves that they are mother and baby, so he gets lashes. If it might nurse a stranger, the relationship is uncertain, and he does not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: To receive lashes (מלקות)
The prohibition against slaughtering an animal and its baby on the same day
He receives lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sign that is good enough for the laws of בכור may not be strong enough to give lashes, which need certainty.

phrases.english: For receiving lashes over it because of 'it and its young.'
If you say it shows mercy to its own,
but to one not its own it does not show mercy — he gets lashes,
but if you say that to one not its own
it also shows mercy — he does not get lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִלְקֵא עֲלַהּ מִשּׁוּם אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8's question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is lashes for אותו ואת בנו when slaughtering a nursing animal and the baby it nurses.

steps.title: A proof from buying an animal from a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the משנה that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds an animal nurses only its own baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the answer? Come and hear: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Someone who buys an animal from a גוי does not need to worry that the baby with it was the baby of another animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that seems to say nursing proves the baby is the animal's own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we don't worry that the nursing baby belongs to another animal, it sounds like an animal nurses only its own young. That would support the second reading in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys
A non-Jew

phrases.english: What is the answer? Come and hear:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who buys an animal from a non-Jew —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת הָיָה.
phrases.english: does not need to worry that perhaps it was the baby of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds an animal nurses only its own young.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one who buys an animal from a גוי does not worry that the baby belongs to another.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof: 'was,' not 'is'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה says 'was,' which means that either way the animal had already given birth, so the ruling works under both readings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'it is'? It says 'it was'! This is what it means: He does not need to worry that perhaps this is another animal's baby, because the animal would not be nursing unless it had a baby of its own from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the wording of the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not claim that the nursing baby is definitely hers. It only says we need not worry about the next baby being a בכור, because nursing shows she gave birth before. That works even if she sometimes nurses a stranger, so the question in step 7 is still not settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach...? This questions the exact wording
This is what it means
From the start, originally

steps.whatToRemember: Nursing at least proves that an animal has given birth before, which is enough to rule out a בכור. Whether nursing proves that a specific baby is hers, which matters for lashes, is not decided by this proof.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'it is'?
It teaches 'it was'!
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת,
phrases.english: he does not need to worry that perhaps it is the baby of another,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה לָהּ וָלָד מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: since it would not nurse unless it had a baby from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The משנה fits both readings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read 'was' as if it said 'is.' The משנה only means the animal already gave birth, not that this baby is definitely hers.

steps.title: Proof from the nursing mothers in the flock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the case of a man who sees first-time mothers and older mothers all nursing in his flock. The ruling is that he does not worry the babies got switched. The גמרא then asks: why not worry that a mother is kindly nursing a baby that isn't hers? This suggests an animal nurses only its own baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A man walked into his flock and saw first-time mothers nursing, and mothers that were not first-timers nursing. He does not need to worry that this one's baby went over to that one, or that that one's baby went over to this one. Why not? We should worry that maybe the mother is just being kind to a stranger's baby!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof that, in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, an animal nurses only its own baby. The proof comes from the case of the nursing mothers in the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If animals sometimes nursed other animals' babies out of kindness, the owner should worry that the babies are mixed up. The ruling says he does not worry. That seems to show an animal nurses only its own baby.

keyTerms.meaning: Mother animals giving birth for the first time
His flock
It really is kind to, it shows real mercy (here: nursing a baby that isn't its own)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one entered into his flock
and saw first-time mothers nursing,
and ones that are not first-time mothers nursing —
he does not worry

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ,
phrases.english: that perhaps the baby of this one came over to that one,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ.
phrases.english: or that perhaps the baby of that one came over to this one.
Why not?
Let us worry that perhaps it is being kind to a stranger's baby!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 11, the גמרא tries a second proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, an animal nurses only its own baby
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the flock with first-time and older mothers nursing, where the owner does not worry about switched babies

steps.title: A mother won't leave her own baby for a stranger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Even if an animal might nurse a stranger, it won't do so when its own baby is right there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where its own baby is present, it does not leave its own baby to show kindness to a baby that isn't its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the flock, every mother has her own baby nearby. So even if animals sometimes nurse strangers, here each mother will feed her own. The ruling doesn't prove anything about a mother with no baby of her own around.

keyTerms.meaning: Where its own (baby) is present
Leaves, abandons
Shows mercy, is kind to

phrases.english: In a place where its own is present,
it does not leave its own
and show kindness to one that is not its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The flock case is special, because each mother's own baby is there, so it shows nothing about a mother whose own baby is not around.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'and similarly'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling 'the matter stays in its status' about buying a nursing animal from a non-Jew. That ruling is followed by 'וכן' ('and similarly'). The גמרא argues that the first clause must be like the second. In the second the baby is surely the mother's own, so in the first it is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The matter stays in its status,' and so on. Isn't the first clause like the last clause? Just as in the last clause the baby is surely its own, so too in the first clause the baby is surely its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third proof, this time from how the two parts of the teaching are linked by the word 'וכן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and similarly' seems to make the two clauses equal. In the last clause the baby is surely the mother's own. So the first clause, a nursing animal bought from a non-Jew, would also mean the baby is surely hers. That fits the view that an animal nurses only its own baby.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter stays in its presumed status
The first clause
The last clause
Similar to, like
Certainly

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'The matter stays in its status,' etc.
Is it not
that the first clause is like the last clause?
Just as in the last clause it is certainly its own,
so too in the first clause it is certainly its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 12 was rejected, the גמרא brings another proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the nursing baby is surely the mother's own
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'וכן' linking the first clause to the last clause in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's teaching

steps.title: The two clauses are different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. Each clause stands on its own. In the last clause the baby is surely the mother's, but in the first clause it may not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from 'and similarly' by saying the two clauses are not about the same situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulings can sit next to each other without being the same in every detail. In the last clause, each mother's own baby is there, so the baby is surely hers. In the first clause, the animal bought from the non-Jew might be nursing a baby that isn't hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a real comparison? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
As it is, on its own terms

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
This one is as it is,
and that one is as it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הַאי כִּדְאִיתֵאּ, וְהַאי כִּדְאִיתֵאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison of the two clauses made in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the first clause must match the last clause in every detail.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the two clauses describe the same situation, but they don't. Only in the last clause is the baby certainly the mother's own.

steps.title: What 'and similarly' really means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the word 'וכן'. It only means both cases share the same result: the mother is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'and similarly' mean? It refers to the exemption from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the obvious question its rejection raises: if the clauses are different, why does it say 'and similarly'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And similarly' does not mean the two cases are the same in every detail. It only means the result is the same: the mother's next baby is not counted as a בכור. Even if the baby she is nursing isn't hers, she would only nurse after already giving birth herself.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly
Exemption
The law of the firstborn animal

steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs fail. The 'היה' wording only shows that the mother gave birth before. The flock case only shows that a mother won't leave her own baby for a stranger. The word 'וכן' only means both mothers are exempt from בכורה. So the question about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view stays open.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the word 'וכן' can link two cases that share a result without making them the same in every detail.

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'and similarly'?
It refers to the exemption from the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection from step 15 by explaining the word 'וכן' that the proof in step 14 relied on.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And similarly' makes the two clauses the same in every detail, so in both the baby is surely the mother's own.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'And similarly' only means both clauses share the same result: exemption from בכורה.

steps.title: A pig-like animal following a ewe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a ewe followed by a pig-like young animal is exempt from בכורה, but the animal may not be eaten until אליהו comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone saw a pig-like animal following a ewe, the ewe is exempt from בכורה. The animal is forbidden to eat 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רבי יוחנן about a strange-looking young animal following a ewe as if it were her baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate rulings here. The ewe is exempt from בכורה, which treats this animal as her baby. Yet the animal itself may not be eaten, which seems to doubt that it is hers. The פסוק at the end suggests the question stays open until אליהו decides it.

keyTerms.meaning: A pig; here, a young animal that looks like a pig
Trailing after, following closely
A ewe (female sheep)
Exempt from בכורה: her next baby is not a firstborn
Until he comes and teaches righteousness to you; used to mean until אליהו decides

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one saw a pig following after a ewe,
phrases.notes: He means a young animal that looks like a pig, following the ewe the way a baby follows its mother.

phrases.english: she is exempt from the firstborn status,
and it is forbidden to eat
"until he comes and teaches righteousness to you."
phrases.notes: הושע 10:12. Here it means: until אליהו comes and settles the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of whether an animal nurses another's baby, the גמרא brings a related ruling about a strange animal following a ewe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ewe is exempt from בכורה. The pig-like animal is forbidden to eat until אליהו comes.

steps.title: The ruling seems to follow two opposing opinions
steps.stepSummary: The exemption follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but the ban on eating follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Exempt from בכורה: whose view is that? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's. Forbidden to eat: that is the view of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling. Its two halves seem to follow two opinions that disagree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל assumes the young animal really belongs to the ewe, so she is exempt from בכורה. The רבנן worry it may not be hers, and then it could be a real pig, so it may not be eaten. You cannot hold both views at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion is this?
The Sages who argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

phrases.english: Exempt from the firstborn status: like whom?
Like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but forbidden to eat, like the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each half of the ruling follows a different side of the dispute, so the ruling contradicts itself.

steps.title: Why quote a פסוק about אליהו?
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling follows the רבנן, the doubt is about the facts. The wording should then have been 'until the matter becomes known to you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, if this follows the רבנן, why say 'until he comes and teaches righteousness to you'? He should have said 'until the matter becomes known to you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge, this one about the wording of the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the only doubt is a factual one: whose baby is this? Facts can be found out without אליהו. The פסוק about אליהו points to a doubt about what the הלכה is, and that does not fit the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds another challenge
Until the matter becomes known to you; a doubt about the facts
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Two different kinds of doubt are being contrasted. 'Until it becomes known to you' is a doubt about the facts. 'Until אליהו comes' is a doubt about what the הלכה is.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is like the Rabbis,
what is the point of "until he comes and teaches righteousness to you"?
He should have said "until the matter becomes known to you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the one in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק quoted at the end of the ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about אליהו implies a doubt about the הלכה. Under the רבנן, the doubt is only about the facts.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יוחנן was unsure which opinion is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן did not know whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן. That would explain the פסוק about אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: he was unsure whether the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, and it is about to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן was unsure of the הלכה, the פסוק fits well, because a doubt in הלכה waits for אליהו. It might also explain why he takes a careful position on each side. The next two steps check whether this answer holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a suggested answer
He is unsure, it is a doubt for him

phrases.english: And if you will say: he is unsure

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: whether the halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
or like the Rabbis,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the challenges of steps 18 and 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seems to mix two opinions and quotes a פסוק that does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי יוחנן was unsure which opinion is the הלכה, and that is why he quotes the פסוק about אליהו.

steps.title: A doubt cannot give a full exemption
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן was unsure, he could not declare the ewe fully exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is unsure, why is she exempt from בכורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone unsure of the הלכה cannot give a clear-cut ruling in either direction. Yet רבי יוחנן plainly says the ewe is exempt, as if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view were certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?

phrases.english: If he is unsure,
why is she exempt from the firstborn status?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אַמַּאי פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggestion of step 20.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being unsure does not fit a definite ruling that the ewe is exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן himself rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said that the הלכה always follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, except in three cases. So he cannot have been unsure here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, was he really unsure? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה, the הלכה is like him, except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stronger rejection of the suggestion in step 20. It uses another statement of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general rule that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה. Only three cases are exceptions, and ours is not one of them. So רבי יוחנן had no doubt, and the original challenges of steps 18 and 19 come back. Step 23 gives a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Is he really unsure?
The הלכה follows him
A guarantor, one of the three exceptions
The 'last proof', another exception

steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן was unsure fails twice. A doubt cannot give a clear exemption, and רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל anyway. So the mixed ruling still needs an explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the famous rule that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, with three exceptions.

phrases.english: And furthermore: is he really unsure?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּמִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
phrases.english: Every place that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught in our Mishnah
the halacha is like him,
except for the guarantor, Tzaidan, and the last proof!
phrases.notes: Three cases found elsewhere: בבא בתרא 174a, גיטין 74a, סנהדרין 31a. Our case isn't one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection of step 20, using רבי יוחנן's own general rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן was unsure of the הלכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן himself rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, so he had no doubt.

steps.title: He knew whose view to follow but not what that view says
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה surely follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The open doubt is whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a mother animal is merciful to a baby that is not her own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he was sure the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. What he was unsure about is whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that an animal that has given birth will show mercy to another's baby, or will not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the challenges from steps 18–19, after the first answer failed in steps 21–22. The doubt was never about whose opinion to follow. It was about what that opinion actually holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that he could not have been unsure whether to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so the גמרא moves the doubt somewhere else. Now the uncertainty is inside רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own view: will a mother nurse a baby that is not hers? This explains the open-ended ruling ('until אליהו comes'), and it still lets him follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to open a fresh answer that keeps the earlier assumption
It was obvious to him
He was in doubt
An animal that has given birth shows mercy, so it may nurse a baby that is not its own

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of doubt. Here he is NOT unsure which תנא to follow. He is unsure what the תנא he follows actually holds.

phrases.english: Actually, it was obvious to him
that the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but he was unsure

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָבַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: whether Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds
that an animal that has given birth is merciful,
or is not merciful.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 22 rejected the idea that he was unsure whose view to follow, this step moves the doubt into the content of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the doubt: from 'whose opinion?' to 'what does that opinion hold?'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He was unsure whether the halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: He surely follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but is unsure whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds יולדת מרחמת.

steps.title: Why not teach the case with a lamb?
steps.stepSummary: If the doubt is about a mother's mercy, the more common case of a lamb should have been taught. That case would also raise the question of lashes for slaughtering a mother and its young.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, instead of teaching us a pig, let him teach us a lamb, and ask about getting lashes for it because of the rule against slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer from step 23. If the doubt is only about a mother's mercy, why use the odd case of a pig?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the question is whether the nursing baby is really this mother's own, the same doubt comes up with an ordinary lamb nursing from a ewe. That case would have practical results for the איסור of אותו ואת בנו, which carries lashes. So choosing the strange pig case seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; it introduces a challenge built on what was just said
Instead of teaching us
A lamb
To receive lashes
The איסור against slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day

phrases.english: If so,
instead of teaching us a pig,
phrases.notes: He means the pig-like animal seen following the ewe in the original ruling.

phrases.english: let him teach us a lamb,
and about being lashed for it
because of "it and its offspring"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן חֲזִיר, לַישְׁמְעִינַן טָלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks step 23's answer by asking why that kind of doubt was shown with a pig.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of a pig as the example in the ruling, given the explanation in step 23
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubt about a mother's mercy would show up more naturally with a lamb. That case has a practical result for אותו ואת בנו, so the pig case seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The pig teaches mercy even toward another species
steps.stepSummary: A lamb case could suggest that a mother shows mercy only to babies of her own species. The pig case teaches that even a baby of another species might be nursed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pig was needed. If he had taught a lamb, I would have said: even if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a mother animal is merciful, that is only toward her own species, not another species. So he taught a pig, to show that she may be merciful even toward another species, since we can say that perhaps she showed mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 24. The pig case teaches something a lamb case could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb case would only raise doubt about babies of the same species. We might then think a ewe would never nurse an animal of a different kind. The pig case shows that, in the doubt about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, even a different-species baby might be nursed out of mercy. So we cannot assume it came from her.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Of its own species
Perhaps

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but it is unclear whether he holds יולדת מרחמת. The pig case teaches that this possible mercy could even reach a baby of another species.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to teach a pig,
for if he had taught us a lamb,
I would have said:
even if you say
that he holds an animal that has given birth is merciful,
that is toward its own species;
toward one not of its species, no.
So he teaches us a pig: that it may be merciful,
even toward one not of its species as well,
since one can say
that perhaps it was merciful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers step 24's challenge by showing that the pig example adds a new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The example adds something: the strange case teaches a wider point than the ordinary one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only a lamb case, we would think a mother's possible mercy reaches only babies of her own species.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pig case shows that the possible mercy may reach even a baby of another species.

steps.title: A teaching of רבי יוחנן that fits this explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to bring a question raised by רבי יוחנן. It fits the explanation that the open doubt is about יולדת מרחמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יוחנן said: a question was asked...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts quoting a question from רבי יוחנן to support the explanation it just gave, and the quote continues on the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והיינו ('and this is') tells us the coming quote matches what was just said. The content of רבי יוחנן's question comes next. It should show that the doubt was about the mother's mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what was meant); it ties a source to the point just made
He asked / a question was raised

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A question was raised

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins bringing support for the explanation reached in steps 23–25.
steps.raayaObject: That the doubt in the ruling was about whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds יולדת מרחמת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A question raised by רבי יוחנן (it continues in the next part of the text)
